subsystems.name: Topological insulator film
subsystems.role: provides protected surface states that conduct electricity while the bulk remains insulating.
parts: bismuth selenide (Bi2Se3) or bismuth telluride (Bi2Te3) crystal

subsystems.name: Substrate
subsystems.role: supports the film and provides a lattice match for high-quality growth.
parts: sapphire, silicon carbide, or strontium titanate
buffer layers such as cadmium telluride

subsystems.name: Electrical contacts
subsystems.role: inject and extract current from the surface states.

subsystems.name: Gate stack
subsystems.role: tunes the Fermi level to isolate surface conduction from bulk conduction.
parts: dielectric layer (aluminium oxide or hexagonal boron nitride)

subsystems.name: Encapsulation
subsystems.role: protects air-sensitive surfaces from oxidation and contamination.

buildSteps.title: Select the material system
buildSteps.detail: Choose a topological insulator with a large bulk band gap and robust surface states, such as Bi2Se3 or a HgTe quantum well.

buildSteps.title: Grow the film
buildSteps.detail: Use molecular beam epitaxy or chemical vapour deposition to grow single-crystal thin films on a lattice-matched substrate, controlling thickness to atomic precision.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the device
buildSteps.detail: For exfoliated flakes, transfer them onto a substrate; for thin films, use lithography and etching to define mesas and isolate devices.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate contacts
buildSteps.detail: Deposit metal electrodes and anneal to form low-resistance contacts to the surface states.

buildSteps.title: Deposit the gate stack
buildSteps.detail: Grow or transfer a thin dielectric layer and deposit a gate electrode to control the surface carrier density.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: Cover the device with an inert layer to prevent oxidation and contamination, which would destroy the protected surface states.

buildSteps.title: Characterise
buildSteps.detail: Measure magnetotransport and use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to confirm surface-state behaviour and bulk insulation.

buildSteps.title: Integrate
buildSteps.detail: Connect the device to circuitry for applications such as low-dissipation interconnects or topological qubits.

prerequisites.why: surface states are only protected in materials with very few defects and impurities.
scattering from contamination and interface defects destroys the protected conduction.
many topological insulators conduct through the bulk, masking the surface states; suppressing this is an active research goal.
using these materials for fault-tolerant qubits requires controlled Majorana modes, not yet demonstrated.

pathway.milestone: research on materials such as Bi2Se3 and HgTe; surface states observed in laboratory experiments
pathway.unlocks: understanding of how spin-orbit coupling protects electron flow.

pathway.milestone: room-temperature, bulk-insulating films with gate-tunable surface conduction
integration with conventional semiconductors or superconducting circuits
pathway.unlocks: hybrid devices that combine topological protection with existing technology.

pathway.milestone: topological qubits and lossless computing architectures
pathway.unlocks: fault-tolerant quantum computing or energy-efficient electronics, if materials and control challenges are solved.
